title: Exact-body preservation: forwarded body text vs the raw upstream text of the same call

method.runner: scratch wrapper that calls the existing _default_runner and retains the raw JSON envelope of the action subprocess
method.comparison_basis: same call only: raw stdout JSON item text vs Trailhead-normalised item text; no second timestamp, no re-fetch, no cached copy
method.public_route: allow_authenticated=False -> registry-selected public backend forced with --backend <label>; isolated empty HOME for the child
method.quota: allow_quota_consuming=False and TRAILHEAD_DISABLE_ASR=1; neither action is a quota action
method.not_stored_here: raw upstream envelopes (176 KB v2ex / 3.7 KB web) and full page text stay in scratch; this ledger keeps hashes, lengths and <=120-char previews

controls_observed.child_home: isolated temporary directory (path not recorded), distinct from the operator home

env.child_env_note: child env is a strict allowlist; the ASR veto is evaluated in the parent process before the subprocess is spawned, so absence here is by design, not a disabled veto

upstream_signals.note: Pinned Agent Reach 1.6.0 (schema_version 1) carries no continuation, truncation or page-cursor field. Continuation is therefore unknown, not complete, and there is no cursor to follow.

limitations: Items are produced by the third-party Agent Reach CLI and forwarded by Trailhead without native scoring or extraction.
Trailhead never installs, configures, updates, or logs in to Agent Reach.
Public-only mode: no authenticated session and no browser fallback were used.
The upstream process ran with a private empty HOME and redirected config/cache variables; that is environment isolation, not a filesystem sandbox, so operator files remain readable by absolute path.
Some upstream raw payloads were dropped to keep output bounded.

env.child_env_note: child env is a strict allowlist; the ASR veto is evaluated in the parent process before the subprocess is spawned, so absence here is by design, not a disabled veto

checks.check: forwarded text equals the raw upstream text of the same call, character for character
character length identical (no silent clip on either side)
equality survives whitespace normalisation (not a re-rendered near-match)
final 200 chars exist, are non-empty, and hash-match upstream
text_truncated is false and body.local_truncated is false
body.upstream_chars == body.returned_chars == len(text) == raw upstream chars
body.upstream_truncated is null and result.upstream.truncated is null
continuation state is 'unknown' with source 'absent' and next_offset null
raw envelope carries schema_version 1 and no 'truncated'/'continuation' field
classify_page_shell returns None for the whole upstream body and the forwarded body
every upstream item was forwarded (no blocked/missing/empty withdrawal)
the old 4000-char slice of the SAME payload differs from what was forwarded (the bound would have cut this artifact)
checks.applies_to: v2ex read (artifact > 4000 chars); web read is 3312 chars, so this check is reported as not exercised rather than passed

not_exercised.old_bound_counterfactual_differs: web read returned 3312 chars, below the old 4000 bound

not_established: Whole-artifact completeness for either read: body.upstream_complete is null and the pinned envelope carries no end-of-artifact or continuation field to validate.
That the upstream text equals the live page: both are upstream renderings (v2ex API model, jina reader for the asyncio page); the comparison is Trailhead forwarding vs upstream output, one hop.
Behaviour above MAX_TOTAL_BODY_CHARS (250000): both artifacts are far below the shared budget, so the mid-body cut and body_budget_exhausted paths are not exercised here.
Parity, freshness or reliability across hosts: one capture per action, one machine, no retry.

That the old 4000-char result would equal the labelled counterfactual slice in a historical run: the slice is derived deterministically from today's payload and is labelled counterfactual, not historical live.
